subject.title: [Security] Unsafe deserialization of incoming WebSocket commands in Gateway

question: Does any accepted Gateway request, including plugin-dispatched parameters, pass attacker-controlled prototype keys into an unsafe assignment or recursive merge sink?
rationale: The report's stated Zod premise and file path do not match current main, but only a security owner should finalize the boundary after checking method-specific and plugin dispatch sinks.

options.title: Verify the full sink path
options.body: Run a private focused probe across parsing, request validation, core dispatch, and plugin dispatch, then close as unsubstantiated if no prototype mutation is observable.

options.title: Harden the identified sink
options.body: If the probe finds an unsafe merge or assignment, reject dangerous keys at that narrow owner boundary and add regression coverage.
